These diffractive processors designed by deep learning have various applications, e.g., all-optical image analysis, feature detection, object classification, computational imaging and seeing through diffusers, also enabling task-specific camera designs and new optical components for spatial, spectral and temporal beam shaping and spatially-controlled wavelength division multiplexing. We demonstrate the efficiency of linear programmable photonic neural networks for low-power optical computing applications. By generating hypervectors with over 100,000 dimensions through optical scattering and integrating them with holographic memory-based computing, we achieve significant improvements in latency and energy consumption compared to electronic and photonic neural networks.
